experiences.name: Diavolezza Glacier Skiing
experiences.description: Experience world-class skiing on the Diavolezza glacier near Pontresina, offering stunning runs with panoramic views of Piz Palü and Bernina peaks. Suitable for intermediate to advanced skiers with over 10km of marked pistes and off-piste opportunities.

experiences.name: Bernina Express Scenic Winter Rail Journey
experiences.description: Board the iconic UNESCO-listed Bernina Express from Poschiavo station, winding through dramatic Alpine landscapes, frozen lakes, and snow-covered viaducts. The route passes the famous Brusio spiral viaduct just minutes from Poschiavo, offering breathtaking winter scenery.
experiences.location: Poschiavo Railway Station, Via Principale, Poschiavo

experiences.name: Cross-Country Skiing on Alp Grüm Trails
experiences.description: Explore serene cross-country ski trails departing from Alp Grüm, a high-altitude stop above Poschiavo accessible by the Bernina railway. Glide through pristine snow with sweeping views of the Palü glacier and the Poschiavo valley below.

experiences.name: Snowshoeing in Val da Camp
experiences.description: Strap on snowshoes and trek through the enchanting Val da Camp side valley near Poschiavo, a quiet and pristine winter wilderness. Guided tours reveal local Alpine flora, frozen waterfalls, and traditional Graubünden stone farmhouses buried in snow.

experiences.name: Traditional Graubünden Fondue & Pizzoccheri Dinner
experiences.description: Warm up after a day on the slopes with an authentic Graubünden dinner in Poschiavo's historic village center. Savor local cheese fondue, hearty Pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta with alpine cheese and vegetables), and Valtellina wines in a cozy centuries-old stone restaurant.
experiences.location: Historic Village Center, Via Principale, Poschiavo

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Cross-Country Skiing on Alp Grüm Trails

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30. Rest and travel day.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich Airport at 22:30. Take the train toward Chur and then connect toward Poschiavo via the Bernina Express route (or arrange a pre-booked budget transfer). Check in to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Unpack and settle in for the night.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.lunch: On the plane or grab a quick bite at Zurich Airport (budget CHF 10–15 at airport kiosks or Migros supermarket inside the terminal).
meals.dinner: Pick up snacks and essentials at a convenience store or vending machine near the train station upon arrival in Poschiavo. Keep it light — CHF 5–10.

day_by_day.notes: The train journey from Zurich to Poschiavo takes approximately 3.5–4 hours with connections. Check SBB (Swiss Federal Railways) for the last available train. Consider booking tickets in advance on the SBB app for the best budget fares. The B&B is located on Via Principale in Poschiavo — confirm late check-in arrangements with the host ahead of time.

day_by_day.morning: After a well-deserved rest, enjoy a leisurely morning at the B&B. Explore the charming historic village of Poschiavo on foot — stroll through the old town, admire the Spanish Quarter (Quartiere Spagnolo) with its colorful Italianate architecture, and visit the main square Piazza Comunale. This is a free and scenic way to orient yourself to the area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the local Poschiavo valley for a beginner-friendly snowshoe walk or a gentle winter hike along the valley floor trails near the village. Rent snowshoes locally if available (approx. CHF 15–20/day rental). The snow-covered landscape around Poschiavo offers stunning views of the surrounding Alps without the cost of a ski pass.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village center and explore the local shops. Relax at the B&B and plan the week ahead using trail maps and local brochures available at the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy the B&B breakfast included with your stay — typically bread, cheese, cold cuts, jam, and coffee/tea.
meals.lunch: Pick up supplies at the local Coop or Migros supermarket in Poschiavo for a self-made picnic lunch in the village square — CHF 8–12.
meals.dinner: Dine at Ristorante Suisse or a local trattoria in Poschiavo. Look for the daily set menu (Menü del giorno) which typically costs CHF 18–25 and includes a starter, main, and sometimes a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Poschiavo is in the Italian-speaking canton of Graubünden, so menus and locals often speak Italian. The village has a relaxed, authentic Swiss-Italian atmosphere. Tuesday is a good day to visit local shops before they get busy on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Take the iconic Bernina Express (Rhaetian Railway) from Poschiavo up to Alp Grüm station — a short but breathtaking ride through UNESCO World Heritage mountain scenery. Alp Grüm sits at 2,091 meters altitude and is the starting point for the featured Cross-Country Skiing on Alp Grüm Trails experience. Arrive early (around 9:00 AM) to make the most of the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the cross-country ski trails from Alp Grüm. The trails wind through serene alpine landscapes with panoramic views of the Palü Glacier and the Valposchiavo valley below. Take breaks to photograph the stunning scenery. The trails are well-marked and suitable for various skill levels.
day_by_day.evening: Take the Bernina Express back down to Poschiavo in the late afternoon. Warm up with a hot drink at a local café in the village before heading back to the B&B.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast before departing.
meals.lunch: Pack a self-prepared lunch from the supermarket to eat on the trails at Alp Grüm — sandwiches, fruit, chocolate, and a thermos of hot tea. CHF 8–10. Note: There is a small mountain restaurant at Alp Grüm (Ristorante Alp Grüm) but it can be pricey — budget CHF 20–30 if you choose to eat there.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at the B&B if kitchen facilities are available, using groceries from Coop/Migros — pasta, sauce, and local cheese for CHF 10–15. Alternatively, try a local pizzeria in Poschiavo for a budget pizza at CHF 15–20.

day_by_day.notes: Cross-country ski equipment can be rented in Poschiavo or sometimes at Alp Grüm. Confirm rental availability and costs (approx. CHF 20–35/day) before heading up. The Bernina Express train ticket from Poschiavo to Alp Grüm is short and relatively affordable — check SBB for exact fares and consider a Swiss Travel Pass if it offers savings over your trip. Dress in warm, waterproof layers as Alp Grüm is significantly colder than the valley.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Bernina Express northward to Pontresina or St. Moritz — two of the most famous winter sports destinations in the Engadin valley, reachable within 30–45 minutes from Poschiavo. In Pontresina, explore the village on foot and visit the free cross-country ski trails in the Engadin valley, which are among the best in Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: In Pontresina or St. Moritz, visit the free public ice rink or watch ski jumping and other winter sports events if any are scheduled (check local event calendars). Walk along the frozen Lake St. Moritz for stunning mountain views — completely free. Browse the village of Pontresina which is more budget-friendly than St. Moritz.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by train in the early evening. Enjoy a quiet evening at the B&B, reviewing photos and planning the remaining days.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast.
meals.lunch: Grab a budget lunch in Pontresina — look for a bakery or Coop/Migros for sandwiches and snacks. CHF 8–12. Avoid the expensive restaurants in St. Moritz center.
meals.dinner: Back in Poschiavo, try Osteria Pozzo in the village for hearty local Graubünden cuisine. Look for dishes like Maluns (potato dish) or Pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta) — budget CHF 18–25 for a main course.

day_by_day.notes: St. Moritz is one of the most expensive resorts in the world — avoid shopping or dining there and instead use it as a scenic backdrop for free activities. Pontresina is a much more budget-friendly alternative nearby. The train pass between Poschiavo and these destinations is the main cost of the day — check if a regional day pass offers better value than individual tickets.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Alp Grüm for a second day of cross-country skiing, this time exploring different trail routes you may have missed on Day 3. The Alp Grüm trail network offers varying difficulty levels — try a longer or more challenging loop if you feel confident. The morning light on the Palü Glacier is particularly spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: After skiing, take a short walk to the viewpoint above Alp Grüm station for panoramic views of the glacier and the valley. On clear days, you can see deep into Italy. Spend time relaxing and soaking in the alpine atmosphere before heading back down.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo and treat yourself to a visit to a local bar or café for an Aperol Spritz or local wine — a budget-friendly way to experience Swiss-Italian culture. CHF 5–8 per drink.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast.
meals.lunch: Pack another trail lunch from the supermarket — energy bars, cheese, bread, and hot drinks in a thermos. CHF 8–10.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at the B&B using local ingredients — try making a simple Rösti (Swiss potato dish) with eggs and local cheese, purchased from the supermarket for CHF 10–15.

day_by_day.notes: Friday may see more visitors heading to the mountains for the weekend — start early to avoid crowds on the trails. If you have a multi-day ski pass or rental agreement, confirm it covers this second day at Alp Grüm. Check weather forecasts the night before as alpine conditions can change rapidly.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Valposchiavo valley by taking a local bus or walking trail south toward Brusio, famous for the UNESCO-listed Brusio Circular Viaduct — a stunning spiral railway bridge. The walk from Poschiavo to Brusio takes approximately 1.5–2 hours through scenic winter landscapes and is completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Brusio Circular Viaduct and watch the Bernina Express trains spiral through the iconic structure — a unique and memorable experience. Walk back toward Poschiavo or take the local bus back. Stop at a local farm shop or market stall if open on Saturday for local cheeses, cured meats, and honey at reasonable prices.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Poschiavo, enjoy a final evening exploring the village. Visit the local church (Chiesa di San Vittore) and the small local museum if open. Have a relaxed dinner celebrating a great week in the Alps.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast.
meals.lunch: Picnic near the Brusio Viaduct with supplies from the supermarket — local bread, cheese, salami, and fruit. CHF 10–12.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last full dinner — try a local restaurant in Poschiavo for a traditional Graubünden meal. Dishes like Capuns (chard-wrapped dumplings) or Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup) are authentic and filling. Budget CHF 25–35 for a two-course meal with a glass of local wine.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is a great day to visit local markets if any are running in Poschiavo or nearby villages. The Brusio Viaduct walk is best done in good weather — check the forecast. This is a good day to purchase any local souvenirs such as Swiss chocolate, local honey, or Graubünden specialties from the Coop or local shops at reasonable prices.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely breakfast at the B&B. Take a last morning walk through Poschiavo village to say goodbye to this beautiful corner of Switzerland. Visit the weekly Sunday market if available, or simply enjoy a final coffee at a local café while watching the village come to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the B&B (confirm checkout time with host). Pack up and begin the journey back toward Zurich or your departure point. Take the Bernina Express northward — the return journey through the Bernina Pass is equally spectacular and a fitting farewell to the Swiss Alps. Connect at Chur or St. Moritz for trains toward Zurich.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Zurich for onward travel or a final night if needed. If departing from Zurich Airport, allow ample time for connections given the scenic but time-consuming mountain railway journey.

meals.breakfast: Final B&B breakfast — enjoy it fully before checking out.
meals.lunch: Pack a travel lunch from the supermarket before departing — sandwiches, fruit, and snacks for the train journey. CHF 8–10.
meals.dinner: If departing from Zurich, grab a budget meal at the airport Migros or a quick-service restaurant. CHF 12–18. Alternatively, enjoy a final Swiss meal at a Zurich train station restaurant.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return train times the night before on the SBB app and book tickets in advance for the best prices. The Bernina Express is a tourist train and can sell out — especially on weekends. Allow extra time for connections as mountain trains run on fixed schedules. Ensure all luggage is packed and nothing is left at the B&B. Take one last look at the Poschiavo valley — it's a hidden gem of the Swiss Alps that few budget travelers discover.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich or Milan Malpensa airport on flight UA at 22:30. Transfer by train or pre-arranged shuttle toward Poschiavo. Check in to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Settle into your room, unpack, and get a good night's rest to prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in transit)
meals.lunch: Not applicable (in transit)
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack or sandwich at the airport or train station during your transfer — airport kiosks or a quick café stop en route to Poschiavo

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives at 22:30, so no sightseeing is planned for Day 1. Confirm your transfer to Poschiavo in advance — the journey from Zurich takes approximately 3–3.5 hours by train (change at Chur and Tirano or via Pontresina). A taxi or private shuttle from the nearest rail hub may be more practical at this late hour. Keep luggage light for easy transit. B&B check-in should be arranged ahead of time for a late arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely start after your late arrival. After breakfast at the B&B, take a gentle orientation walk through Poschiavo's charming historic village center — explore the Piazza Comunale, admire the Italianate architecture, and get your bearings in this unique Swiss-Italian border town. Visit the local tourist office to pick up trail maps and ski passes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snowshoeing in Val da Camp — strap on snowshoes (rentable in Poschiavo village) and explore the enchanting Val da Camp side valley. This quiet, forested valley offers a peaceful introduction to the alpine landscape without the intensity of a full ski day. The trail winds through snow-covered meadows and pine forests with stunning mountain backdrops — perfect for easing into the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Graubünden Fondue & Pizzoccheri Dinner in Poschiavo's historic village. Warm up with a hearty cheese fondue or the regional buckwheat pasta dish Pizzoccheri — a Valtellina specialty beloved on both sides of the Swiss-Italian border. Enjoy the cozy atmosphere of a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — enjoy local bread, cheese, cold cuts, and coffee included with your stay
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or light snack from a local bakery in Poschiavo before heading to Val da Camp — try a local panino or pastry (budget-friendly, CHF 8–12)
meals.dinner: Traditional Graubünden Fondue & Pizzoccheri Dinner at a local Poschiavo restaurant such as Ristorante Suisse or a similar village trattoria (mid-range, CHF 30–45 per person including a glass of local Valtellina wine)

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoe rentals are available in Poschiavo for approximately CHF 15–20/day. Val da Camp is accessible by local bus or a short drive from the village. This is a recovery and acclimatization day — altitude in Poschiavo is around 1,014m, so take it easy before heading to higher elevations later in the week. Dress in warm layers and waterproof boots.

day_by_day.morning: Diavolezza Glacier Skiing — take the Bernina Express or local RhB train from Poschiavo up toward Pontresina/Diavolezza station (approximately 45–60 min). Board the Diavolezza cable car and enjoy world-class glacier skiing at 3,000m+. Morning snow conditions are typically best — carve through wide open glacier runs with breathtaking views of Piz Palü and Piz Bernina. Ski passes and equipment rental available on-site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Diavolezza — explore the famous Diavolezza-Lagalb ski area. Try the iconic off-piste glacier descent toward Morteratsch if conditions and skill level allow (guided option recommended). Take a mid-afternoon break at the Diavolezza mountain restaurant terrace to soak in the panoramic alpine views over a hot drink.
day_by_day.evening: Return by train to Poschiavo. Rest and freshen up at the B&B. Head out for a relaxed dinner in the village, enjoying the quiet, authentic atmosphere of this lesser-known Swiss gem.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at B&B before departing for Diavolezza
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Diavolezza mountain restaurant — enjoy rösti, soup, or a hot pasta dish with stunning glacier views (mid-range mountain dining, CHF 20–30 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local Poschiavo restaurant — try Osteria Salis or a similar spot for regional pasta, risotto, or grilled meats paired with local Graubünden wine (CHF 28–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Diavolezza ski pass costs approximately CHF 60–70/day for adults. Equipment rental (skis, boots, poles) is available at Diavolezza or in Pontresina for CHF 40–55/day. The RhB train from Poschiavo to Ospizio Bernina/Diavolezza station runs regularly — check the timetable at rhb.ch. Dress in full ski gear with UV protection — glacier altitude means intense sun reflection. Book ski lessons in advance if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Bernina Express Scenic Winter Rail Journey — board the iconic UNESCO-listed Bernina Express from Poschiavo station. Wind through dramatic alpine scenery including the famous Brusio spiral viaduct, snow-blanketed Alp Grüm, the frozen Lago Bianco, and the Bernina Pass at 2,253m. Travel up to St. Moritz or Pontresina for a morning of exploration in the glamorous Engadin valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore St. Moritz or Pontresina on foot — browse the upscale village of St. Moritz, visit the Engadin Museum, or take a scenic winter walk along the frozen Lake St. Moritz. Alternatively, rent cross-country skis in Pontresina and enjoy a short loop on the Engadin's famous Nordic trails. Return to Poschiavo by train in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Poschiavo — explore the village's Spanish Quarter (a unique neighborhood built by returning emigrants from Spain), visit the local church, and enjoy a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at B&B before boarding the morning train
meals.lunch: Lunch in St. Moritz or Pontresina — try a local café or mountain bistro for a mid-range meal such as Engadiner Nusstorte (walnut tart), soup, and a warm drink (CHF 20–35 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at B&B or a nearby Poschiavo restaurant — opt for a lighter meal such as local soup, salad, and regional cheese plate (CHF 20–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express is a highlight of any Swiss Alps trip — book your seat reservation in advance at sbb.ch (reservation fee CHF 10–15; rail pass or point-to-point ticket required). The full Poschiavo–St. Moritz segment takes approximately 1.5 hours. This is a lower-intensity day ideal for mid-week recovery. The Bernina Express panoramic cars offer floor-to-ceiling windows — sit on the right side heading uphill for the best views of the Brusio viaduct.

day_by_day.morning: Cross-Country Skiing on Alp Grüm Trails — take the RhB train from Poschiavo up to Alp Grüm station (a stunning high-altitude stop perched above the valley). Strap on cross-country skis and explore the serene Nordic trails that wind through pristine alpine terrain with sweeping views over the Poschiavo valley and the Palü glacier. The trails are well-groomed and suitable for intermediate skiers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue cross-country skiing or switch to snowshoeing around the Alp Grüm area. Enjoy the extraordinary solitude and silence of this high-altitude landscape — a stark contrast to the busier downhill resorts. Head back down to Poschiavo by mid-afternoon train.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a relaxing evening — consider a visit to a local spa or wellness facility if available, or simply unwind at the B&B with a book. Head out for a celebratory mid-trip dinner with a bottle of local Valtellina Superiore red wine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at B&B before heading to Alp Grüm
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the B&B or a local bakery — enjoy it outdoors at Alp Grüm with panoramic mountain views (self-catered, CHF 5–10)
meals.dinner: Special mid-trip dinner at one of Poschiavo's better restaurants — try a three-course meal with local specialties such as barley soup, venison ragù, and Engadiner Nusstorte for dessert (CHF 40–55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Cross-country ski rentals are available in Poschiavo or at Alp Grüm for approximately CHF 20–30/day. A Nordic trail pass may be required (CHF 10–15). Alp Grüm is accessible only by train — no road access — making it a uniquely peaceful destination. Temperatures at Alp Grüm (2,091m) can be significantly colder than Poschiavo, so dress in extra warm layers. Check train schedules carefully as service frequency may be reduced in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Diavolezza for a second day of downhill skiing — now more familiar with the mountain, push yourself to explore more challenging runs or take a guided off-piste tour on the glacier. Saturday mornings can be busier, so aim to be on the first cable car. Focus on runs you may have missed on Day 3 and enjoy the confidence that comes with a second visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski until early afternoon, then descend and take the train back toward Poschiavo. Stop at Ospizio Bernina (Bernina Pass) for a short winter walk around the frozen Lago Bianco — a hauntingly beautiful high-altitude lake straddling the European watershed. Snap photos of the iconic red Bernina Express trains crossing the snowy landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Poschiavo — explore any remaining corners of the village, pick up local souvenirs (Poschiavo honey, local grappa, or Bündner Fleisch dried meat), and enjoy a farewell dinner with the full Traditional Graubünden experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at B&B before heading to Diavolezza
meals.lunch: Lunch at Diavolezza mountain restaurant or a packed lunch eaten on the slopes (CHF 20–30 or self-catered)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Poschiavo — return to your favorite restaurant from the week or try somewhere new; order a full Graubünden spread with fondue, local charcuterie, and regional desserts paired with Valtellina wine (CHF 35–50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is typically the busiest day at Swiss ski resorts due to weekend visitors — arrive at Diavolezza early (first cable car around 8:30am) to beat the crowds. Consider purchasing a 2-day ski pass combining Days 3 and 6 for a discount (check diavolezza.ch for current pricing). The Lago Bianco stop at Ospizio Bernina is a free and easily accessible highlight — trains stop here on the Bernina line.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Poschiavo — enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the B&B. Take a slow farewell walk through the village, revisit the Piazza Comunale, and perhaps stop for a final espresso at a local café. Pack and check out of the B&B. If time allows, browse the Sunday morning atmosphere of the village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin your return journey — depart Poschiavo by train toward your departure airport (Zurich or Milan Malpensa). The scenic Bernina Express route offers one last breathtaking alpine farewell as you descend through the Engadin and onward. Enjoy the views and reflect on an incredible week in the Swiss Alps.
day_by_day.evening: Travel day — airport transfer and departure. Enjoy a final Swiss meal at the airport or train station before your flight home.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — savor the last of the local Swiss-Italian hospitality
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in Poschiavo before departure, or a snack on the train (CHF 10–20)
meals.dinner: Airport or train station dining — treat yourself to a final Swiss chocolate, Gruyère sandwich, or a sit-down meal at the airport (CHF 20–40 depending on venue)

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at the B&B is typically 10:00–11:00am — confirm with the host. Plan your train connections carefully: Poschiavo to Zurich Airport takes approximately 3.5–4 hours with connections at Tirano or Pontresina and Chur. For Milan Malpensa, travel via Tirano and take the Trenord regional train (approximately 2.5–3 hours total). Book train tickets in advance at sbb.ch for the best fares. Leave extra buffer time for international connections. Don't forget to pick up Swiss chocolate and local Graubünden specialties as gifts before departing!

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer from airport to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama via private luxury transfer (pre-arranged). Check-in, unwind, and enjoy a welcome drink prepared by the host.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night arrival at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Light welcome snack or charcuterie board arranged by the property. Review the week's itinerary and prepare ski gear for the days ahead. Early rest recommended.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — arrival day
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in transit
meals.dinner: Pre-arranged welcome charcuterie board and local Graubünden cheeses at the B&B upon arrival, paired with a glass of Valtellina red wine

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private luxury transfer in advance from Zurich or Milan Malpensa airport to Poschiavo — the drive is approximately 2.5–3 hours. Confirm late check-in with the B&B. Pack ski gear in accessible luggage for an early start the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely gourmet breakfast at the B&B with panoramic Alpine views. After breakfast, take a private transfer or the scenic Bernina Express train up to Pontresina to begin your Diavolezza Glacier Skiing experience. Ride the Diavolezza cable car to 2,978m and enjoy world-class glacier runs with breathtaking views of Piz Palü and Piz Bernina. Morning snow conditions are typically pristine — ideal for first runs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Diavolezza, exploring the legendary Diavolezza-Lagalb ski area. Consider hiring a private mountain guide for personalized off-piste routes and glacier touring. Enjoy a mid-afternoon break at the Berghaus Diavolezza mountain restaurant, one of the finest high-altitude dining spots in the Engadin.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by private transfer. Freshen up at the B&B before heading into the historic village center for a Traditional Graubünden Fondue & Pizzoccheri Dinner. Savor authentic local specialties including Pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta with alpine cheese and greens) and a rich cheese fondue, paired with regional Graubünden wines.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet Alpine breakfast at B&B Berninahaus — fresh bread, local jams, Graubünden cold cuts, eggs, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Berghaus Diavolezza mountain restaurant — premium Alpine lunch with panoramic glacier views; try the Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup) and grilled meats
meals.dinner: Traditional Graubünden Fondue & Pizzoccheri Dinner at a top-rated Poschiavo village restaurant — reserve in advance for a private dining experience

day_by_day.notes: Book a private ski instructor or mountain guide for the Diavolezza glacier in advance — highly recommended for safety on glacier terrain. Lift passes for the Diavolezza-Lagalb area can be purchased as a day pass. Dress in premium technical ski layers; temperatures at 2,978m can be well below -10°C.

day_by_day.morning: After a hearty breakfast, embark on the iconic Bernina Express Scenic Winter Rail Journey from Poschiavo station. Board the UNESCO-listed panoramic train and wind through dramatic Alpine landscapes — frozen viaducts, snow-laden forests, and the spectacular Brusio spiral viaduct. Travel up through Alp Grüm and onward toward St. Moritz or Tirano, soaking in the cinematic winter scenery from heated panoramic carriages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark at Alp Grüm (2,091m) and transition into the Cross-Country Skiing on Alp Grüm Trails experience. Explore serene, groomed cross-country ski trails through high-altitude snowscapes with sweeping views over the Poschiavo valley and the Palü glacier. Rent premium Nordic ski equipment if needed. The trails offer a peaceful contrast to the intensity of downhill skiing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo via the Bernina Express. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the B&B with a private in-room wine and cheese tasting featuring curated Graubünden and Valtellina selections. Optional: visit the historic Palazzo Mengotti or stroll through Poschiavo's beautifully preserved Spanish-style piazza by night.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the B&B — Alpine yogurt, granola, smoked salmon, artisan pastries, and premium espresso
meals.lunch: Ristorante Alp Grüm at the mountain station — a legendary high-altitude dining spot with stunning glacier views; enjoy hearty Alpine soups, rösti, and warm drinks
meals.dinner: Private in-room wine and cheese tasting at the B&B, curated with local Poschiavo cheeses, Valtellina Sforzato wine, and artisan breads — arranged through the host

day_by_day.notes: Book first-class panoramic seats on the Bernina Express well in advance — they sell out quickly in peak winter season. The Alp Grüm stop requires coordination with train schedules; confirm return times. Cross-country ski rentals are available at Alp Grüm or can be arranged through the B&B.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, head to Val da Camp for a premium Snowshoeing in Val da Camp experience. Strap on high-quality snowshoes and trek through the enchanting, untouched side valley near Poschiavo. The valley is a hidden gem — silent, pristine, and dramatically beautiful in winter. Hire a private nature guide to learn about the local Alpine ecosystem, wildlife tracks, and Graubünden mountain culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the snowshoe trek deeper into Val da Camp, reaching elevated viewpoints with sweeping panoramas of the surrounding peaks. Enjoy a private picnic lunch prepared by the B&B — a luxury hamper with local specialties, thermos of hot soup, and mulled wine served in the snow. Return to the trailhead by mid-afternoon and transfer back to the B&B for a premium spa recovery session (arrange a private massage therapist through the host).
day_by_day.evening: Dress for a premium dinner experience in Poschiavo's historic village. Visit one of the finest local restaurants for a multi-course tasting menu featuring Graubünden cuisine elevated with modern Alpine techniques — think venison tartare, truffle-laced Pizzoccheri, and local cheese plates. Pair with a curated wine flight.

meals.breakfast: Full Alpine breakfast at the B&B — warm porridge with mountain honey, fresh fruit, Graubünden cold cuts, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Luxury private picnic hamper in Val da Camp — prepared by the B&B with local cheeses, cured meats, sourdough bread, hot Bündner Gerstensuppe in a thermos, and mulled wine
meals.dinner: Multi-course tasting menu at a premium Poschiavo restaurant — reserve the chef's table for an intimate, personalized dining experience with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Val da Camp is best accessed by car or private transfer from Poschiavo — approximately 10–15 minutes. The snowshoe trails are suitable for all fitness levels but can be extended for more adventurous guests. A private guide enhances the experience significantly. Book the in-room massage therapist 24 hours in advance through the B&B host.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Diavolezza Glacier Skiing area for a second day on the slopes, this time focusing on the Lagalb ski area — a more challenging, less-crowded terrain ideal for advanced skiers. Begin with a private ski coaching session to refine technique on steep groomed runs and mogul fields. The morning light on the Bernina massif from the slopes is extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, explore the Morteratsch glacier area near Pontresina — a short transfer from Diavolezza. Take a guided glacier walk or ski touring excursion with a certified mountain guide, venturing onto the lower reaches of the Morteratsch glacier for a truly immersive high-Alpine experience. This is a rare, exclusive activity that few visitors access.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo for a celebratory evening. Enjoy aperitivo hour at the B&B with Prosecco and local antipasti, followed by a premium dinner at a Poschiavo restaurant specializing in Italian-Swiss fusion cuisine — reflecting the unique cultural blend of this Romansh and Italian-speaking valley.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the B&B — eggs Benedict with smoked Alpine trout, fresh pastries, fruit salad, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Berghaus Diavolezza or Lagalb mountain restaurant — premium Alpine lunch; try the Engadiner Nusstorte (walnut tart) for dessert
meals.dinner: Italian-Swiss fusion tasting menu at a top Poschiavo restaurant — featuring dishes like saffron risotto with local venison, handmade pasta, and a premium Valtellina wine selection

day_by_day.notes: The Lagalb ski area requires a separate lift pass or is included in the Diavolezza-Lagalb combined pass — confirm at the ticket office. Glacier walking requires crampons and a certified guide — arrange through a Pontresina-based mountain guide service. Weather conditions on the glacier can change rapidly; always follow guide instructions.

day_by_day.morning: A slower, indulgent morning — sleep in and enjoy an extended gourmet breakfast at the B&B. Take a leisurely private guided walk through Poschiavo's historic village center, exploring the Spanish-style piazza, the 17th-century Palazzo de Bassus, and the unique architectural heritage that reflects the village's prosperous silk-trading past. Visit a local artisan shop for premium Graubünden souvenirs — handcrafted chocolates, local spirits, and alpine textiles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Bernina Express to St. Moritz for an exclusive afternoon experience in one of the world's most glamorous ski resorts. Explore the Corviglia ski area with a private ski guide, enjoy the legendary St. Moritz après-ski scene, or visit the Badrutt's Palace Hotel for afternoon tea. Browse luxury boutiques on the Via Serlas before returning to Poschiavo on the evening train.
day_by_day.evening: Final premium dinner in Poschiavo — a special farewell meal at the best restaurant in the village. Request a private dining room or chef's table experience. Celebrate the week with a bottle of aged Sforzato di Valtellina DOCG wine and a full tasting menu of Graubünden and Italian Alpine specialties. End the evening with a nightcap of local Grappa at the B&B.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury breakfast at the B&B — full spread including smoked fish, artisan cheeses, fresh-baked croissants, bircher muesli, and a Champagne mimosa
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium St. Moritz restaurant or mountain hut on Corviglia — consider Mathis Food Affairs or Restaurant Marmite for an iconic St. Moritz dining experience
meals.dinner: Farewell tasting menu at Poschiavo's finest restaurant — private dining room, chef's table, full wine pairing with Sforzato di Valtellina DOCG, and a Grappa digestif

day_by_day.notes: St. Moritz is approximately 45 minutes from Poschiavo by Bernina Express — check train schedules carefully to ensure a comfortable return in the evening. In St. Moritz, a private ski guide can be arranged through the Corviglia ski school. Book the farewell dinner well in advance and communicate any dietary preferences to the chef.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the B&B with panoramic views of the Bernina massif. Take a short, gentle morning walk around the Poschiavo lake (Lago di Poschiavo) — a serene, beautiful setting in winter with the snow-capped peaks reflected in the partially frozen lake. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, consider one final short activity — a brief snowshoe loop near the village, a visit to the Poschiavo market (if Sunday market is active), or simply relax at the B&B with a final coffee and Alpine views. Private luxury transfer departs for the airport (Zurich or Milan Malpensa) — allow 2.5–3 hours travel time plus airport check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Carry the memories of a world-class Alpine week — glacier skiing, scenic rail journeys, snowshoeing in pristine valleys, and exceptional Graubünden cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at the B&B — a special send-off spread with the host's signature dishes, local honey, artisan pastries, and a farewell Champagne toast
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Poschiavo café before departure — try Café del Dazio or a local bakery for a final Graubünden pastry and espresso
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining — consider purchasing premium local provisions (Graubünden dried meats, chocolates, Grappa) from Poschiavo shops to enjoy en route

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private transfer booking the evening before departure. Allow extra time if departing via Milan Malpensa due to potential border crossing delays. The Poschiavo lake walk is approximately 45 minutes at a gentle pace and requires only light winter boots — no snowshoes needed. Consider purchasing a bottle of Sforzato di Valtellina as a premium take-home gift.
